title: Chicken Vesuvio
subtitle: Chicago roast chicken with potatoes, white wine, and peas
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces and potato wedges roasted together in olive oil, white wine, and garlic until the skin is crisp and the pan juices are rich and winey. A Chicago Italian staple.
sourceNotes: Chicago Italian-American restaurant classic, associated with the city's Italian steakhouses since the mid-20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Season the chicken up to 24 hours ahead and keep uncovered in the fridge for crispier skin.

content.text: Chicken Vesuvio is a one-pan supper built on a generous pour of white wine and olive oil. Browning the chicken before roasting is not optional; it sets the colour and gives the pan juices their depth. Add the peas only in the last few minutes so they stay bright.
Heat the oven to 200C. Season the chicken pieces all over with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 5 minutes until deep gold. Turn and cook 2 minutes more. Transfer to the roasting tin.
Toss the potato wedges and garlic cloves in the remaining olive oil with the oregano. Scatter around the chicken in the tin.
Pour the white wine and chicken stock into the tin. Tuck in the rosemary sprigs. Roast for 45 minutes.
Scatter the peas over the tin. Return to the oven for 5 minutes until the peas are just cooked and the chicken is cooked through with no pink at the bone.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the tin. Rest for 10 minutes before serving straight from the tin with the pan juices spooned over.

items.symptom: The chicken skin is pale and soft.
items.cause: Not browned before roasting, or the tin was overcrowded.
items.fix: Always brown skin-down first and give each piece space in the tin.

items.symptom: The potatoes are still hard when the chicken is done.
items.cause: The wedges were cut too thick.
items.fix: Cut wedges no more than 3cm at the widest point so they cook at the same rate as the chicken.

items.symptom: The pan juices have dried up.
items.cause: The tin ran dry during roasting.
items.fix: Add a splash more stock or water halfway through if the liquid looks low.
